_comment: Consumption Logic App for the Auto FNOL Triage email-trigger pipeline. Uses the Office 365 Outlook connector's managed trigger over the public Office365 API - no VNet/Private Endpoint involved. All Foundry/Teams calls are plain HTTPS actions against public endpoints with Entra ID auth via a Managed Identity or the HTTP action's OAuth settings.

orchestratorAgentIdFilePlaceholder.defaultValue: <paste orchestrator_agent_id.txt content here, or resolve via Key Vault>

errorNotificationEmail._comment: Recipient for failure notifications. Non-technical Teams channel members must NEVER see partial/failed analyses - any failure anywhere in this workflow (Foundry run failure, HTTP errors, etc.) skips all Teams posting and instead emails full error detail here, then terminates the run as Failed.

workiqBaseUrl._comment: Work IQ web app base URL - also used to post Teams messages (see /post-new-case-alert, /post-case-reply) via the dedicated Agent Identity's delegated auth, since Microsoft Graph has NO app-only permission for posting Teams channel messages (ChannelMessage.Send does not exist as an application permission - see docs/OBO_Bot_Teams_Design.docx and FNOL_Logicapps_Solution_Status.docx section 4.6). A direct Managed-Identity HTTP call to Graph's /messages endpoint (the pre-Agent-Identity approach) cannot work for this step.

workiqApiKey._comment: Matches the WORKIQ_API_KEY app setting on app-autofnol-workiq - resolve via Key Vault reference in production, never hardcode.

$connections._comment: Required declaration for any Consumption Logic App that uses an ApiConnection trigger/action (the Office 365 'When a new email arrives' trigger below) - ARM rejects the deployment if this parameter is not declared here, even though its value is always supplied at deploy time via deploy_logic_apps.py / connections.json.

Try_process_case._comment: All case-processing actions run inside this Try scope. If ANY action fails (HTTP error, timeout, etc.), Logic Apps marks this scope Failed and control passes to Catch_and_notify_failure below - no Teams post ever happens on failure. A successful Foundry run that itself reports status 'failed' is also detected explicitly (see Check_run_failed) and routed to the same failure/email path.

Compute_stable_case_id._comment: Stable, idempotent CaseId derived from internetMessageId per docs/teams-concurrency-design.md step 5 - safe to retry without creating duplicate cases/threads.

Validate_run_completed._comment: Purely cosmetic/diagnostic: forces THIS action to show red/Failed in run history whenever the Foundry run's final status is anything other than 'completed' (e.g. 'failed', 'expired', 'cancelled', or the Until loop's own timeout), since Get_run_status itself always shows Succeeded (the HTTP call worked - it's the payload's status field that indicates failure). Check_run_failed below still performs the actual failure routing/emailing regardless of this action's outcome.

Check_run_failed._comment: Until_run_completes exits Succeeded on EITHER 'completed' or 'failed' Foundry run status (both are HTTP 200s, so the Logic App action itself never fails) - or after a 10-minute timeout. Anything other than 'completed' (failed, timed out, cancelled, expired) routes here: send the detailed failure email directly and terminate the run as Failed WITHOUT ever posting to Teams. Only a genuinely 'completed' run reaches Post_new_case_alert_to_Teams.

body.Subject: [Auto FNOL Triage] Case processing FAILED - @{triggerBody()?['subject']}
body.Body:
The Auto FNOL Triage email-intake Logic App's Foundry agent run did not complete successfully. No message was posted to Teams.

Original email subject: @{triggerBody()?['subject']}

From: @{triggerBody()?['from']}

Internet Message Id: @{triggerBody()?['internetMessageId']}

Foundry thread id: @{body('Parse_thread_id')?['id']}

Final run status: @{body('Get_run_status')?['status']}

Last error:

@{string(body('Get_run_status')?['last_error'])}

runError.message: Foundry run final status: @{body('Get_run_status')?['status']}. Failure notification emailed to @{parameters('errorNotificationEmail')}.

inputs._comment: Creates a NEW top-level channel message = a new reply-chain root for this case, per docs/teams-concurrency-design.md step 1. MUST go through the Work IQ web app's Agent-Identity-backed endpoint, NOT a direct Managed-Identity Graph call - Graph has no app-only permission for posting Teams channel messages (see FNOL_Logicapps_Solution_Status.docx section 4.6).

Idempotent insert keyed on CaseId (PK) - see shared/case_thread_store_schema.sql. MUST go through the Work IQ web app's Agent-Identity-backed /insert-case-thread-map endpoint (pyodbc + Entra token auth), NOT the standard SQL ApiConnection connector - the Fabric SQL Database only accepts Entra-token auth (SQL_COPT_SS_ACCESS_TOKEN), which the Logic App SQL connector does not support directly without OBO, defeating the purpose of the Agent Identity approach.

Catch_and_notify_failure._comment: Runs ONLY if Try_process_case failed (any HTTP error, or the explicit Terminate from Check_run_failed above). Sends a detailed error email to the FNOL solution owner via the same authenticated office365-1 mailbox connection used by the trigger, then fails the overall Logic App run so it is clearly flagged as Failed in run history/alerts. No Teams message is ever sent on this path.

body.Subject: [Auto FNOL Triage] Case processing FAILED - @{triggerBody()?['subject']}
body.Body:
The Auto FNOL Triage email-intake Logic App failed to process an incoming case and did NOT post anything to Teams.

Original email subject: @{triggerBody()?['subject']}

From: @{triggerBody()?['from']}

Internet Message Id: @{triggerBody()?['internetMessageId']}

Workflow run: @{workflow()?['run']?['name']}

Failure details:

@{string(result('Try_process_case'))}

runError.message: Case processing failed - see notification email sent to the FNOL solution owner for full error detail. No message was posted to Teams.
